full_judgment: 12. I have heard the learned Advocates at length and perused the records. The whole argument of the learned Advocate for the opposite parties was that once a tenancy is denied by a tenant claiming an independent title in the self same property, the petitioners ought to have filed a full fledged suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. Repelling the above contention, Mr. Rahim has rightly argued that parties' right is to be determined at a time when the suit is instituted or when a course of action arises. In elaborating this point Mr. Rahim has pointed out that the plaintiffs' claim in suit property by way of purchase on 29.3.63 and the original defendant who was already in the suit land as tenant of the ex-owner, executed a tenancy agreement Ext. 2 with the petitioners on and from 1st Ashar 1370 BS that is, from the year 1963, and he also paid rent for some time admitting the petitioners (plaintiffs) as his landlord. The fact remains that the original defendants had no title whatsoever at that time.
